jurisdiction.name: Zambia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Zambia's AI governance rests on the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024-2026 of the Ministry of Technology and Science, which promises a National AI Council, AI ethics guidelines, regulatory sandboxes and an AI mandate for the communications regulator ZICTA; none of these has yet been set up by any instrument. The Data Protection Act 2021 regulates automated decisions and profiling, and the Securities and Exchange Commission's 2020 sandbox guidelines name AI as a category of innovation that can be tested. A replacement data protection bill covering AI has been announced but not published.
lead_institutions: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026, but the technology ministry's, Parliament's, the communications regulator's and the data protection commissioner's websites could not be accessed. The AI strategy and the data protection law are therefore recorded from official addresses without their text being read on an official site. Zambia is marked for a later retry and, as a country of over 20 million people with few records, for a longer catch-up pass.

instruments.current_status: Zambia's first national AI strategy, covering 2024-2026. The cover gives the period 2024-2026 while the page headers of the same file read '2025 - 2027'; the official ministry site could not be reached to confirm the issued version or an exact publication date (launch reported in non-official sources as November 2024). The strategy announces a National AI Council, sector Technical Working Groups, a National Emerging Technologies Centre of Excellence, AI ethics guidelines and regulatory and data sandboxes, and proposes extending ZICTA's mandate to AI regulation; no implementing instrument for these was found.
instruments.summary: Zambia's first national AI strategy, issued by the Ministry of Technology and Science with a foreword by the Minister, sets a vision of Zambia as a destination for 'AI for Emerging Economies' and strategic pillars on policy and regulation, human capital and AI literacy, digital infrastructure and data, research and innovation, and sector adoption (health, agriculture, education, mining, climate, public services). For governance it proposes a National AI Council advising the ministry, sector Technical Working Groups, Smart Zambia coordinating AI adoption across government and a Centre of Excellence, and it calls for national AI ethics guidelines, regulatory and data sandboxes and extending the ZICTA regulator's mandate to AI regulation and ethical compliance. It includes a phased implementation plan and a monitoring and evaluation framework.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: The only national AI-specific policy document; anchors Zambia's planned AI governance structure and regulatory agenda.

instruments.current_status: Act No. 3 of 2021 (assent 23 March 2021; dated 24 March 2021 in the Act). Commencement is recorded on ZambiaLII as 1 April 2021 by the Data Protection Act (Commencement) Order, 2021 (S.I. 22 of 2021), not confirmed on an official site. Cabinet was reported (non-official sources, 24 April 2025) to have approved in principle a bill to repeal and replace the Act to cover AI, machine learning and data analytics; no bill text was found (see leads).
instruments.summary: Zambia's general data protection law, establishing the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner, principles for processing personal data, registration of data controllers and processors, and data subject rights. Section 62 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects (except for contract, written law or explicit consent, with safeguards including human intervention and the right to contest), and bars automated processing of sensitive personal data without express consent, public interest or a legal basis with safeguards. Data protection impact assessments are required where automated processing, including profiling, produces legal or similarly significant effects.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: The only binding Zambian law with explicit rules on automated decision-making and profiling; governs personal data used to train and run AI systems.

instruments.official_title: Regulatory Sandbox Guidelines for Capital Markets (Guideline No. 3 of 2020)
instruments.english_title: Regulatory Sandbox Guidelines for Capital Markets (Guideline No. 3 of 2020)
instruments.current_status: Dated 9 December 2020; published on the SEC guidelines page (current PDF uploaded May 2026). It is a general fintech sandbox in which 'Artificial Intelligence' is one of the listed application categories and AI is named in the definition of 'innovation'; it has no AI-specific requirements. Gazette listings suggest a 2026 notice of the guidelines (Gazette of 8 May 2026), not reviewed.
instruments.summary: Securities and Exchange Commission guideline, issued under its Securities Act mandate, creating a regulatory sandbox in which capital-market innovations can be live-tested under conditions and limitations designed to protect investors, without full adherence to all regulatory obligations. It defines eligible innovations to include artificial intelligence and automated investment advice and lists 'Artificial Intelligence' among the admissible application categories, and sets eligibility criteria and five stages (application, preparation, testing, exit, commercial deployment) with revocation and oversight rules.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regulatory sandbox that expressly admits AI-based capital-market innovations for supervised testing.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): SEC guideline page and 20-page PDF read (pdftotext); dated 9 December 2020 in the document.
